title: Demonstrate an understanding of contracts and their sources

lessons.title: What is a contract?
lessons.html:
An agreement the law will protect

A contract is an agreement between two or more people that the law will enforce. Each side promises to do something. If one side does not keep the promise, the other side can go to court or to another body for help.

You make contracts every day. When you buy bread at the shop, you agree to pay and the shop agrees to give you the bread. When you start work on a farm, you and the farmer agree that you will work and the farmer will pay you. That is an employment contract.

What makes a contract valid?

For a contract to be valid, these things must be true:

  1. Agreement: both sides agree to the same thing. One side makes an offer and the other side accepts it.
  2. Capacity: the people must be allowed to make contracts. Young children, for example, usually need a parent to help.
  3. Legal: what you agree to do must be allowed by law. A contract to sell stolen cattle is not valid.
  4. Possible: it must be possible to do what was promised.
  5. Formalities: some contracts must be in writing and signed. A contract to buy land must be in writing.

Spoken or written

Many contracts can be spoken (verbal). But a spoken contract is hard to prove if there is a fight later. A written contract is better because everyone can read exactly what was agreed. Always read a contract before you sign. If you do not understand it, ask someone you trust to explain it in your own language.

Example

Sipho agrees with a neighbour to plough his field for R1 500. They shake hands. This is a verbal contract. If they write it down and both sign, it is much easier to prove later.

lessons.title: Where contract law comes from and contracts on the farm
lessons.html:
Sources of contract law

The rules about contracts come from different places. These places are called the sources of law.

  • Common law: old rules that have been used for a very long time. In South Africa our common law comes from Roman-Dutch law. Most basic contract rules come from here.
  • Legislation: laws made by Parliament. For example, the Basic Conditions of Employment Act sets minimum rules for work contracts, and the Consumer Protection Act protects people who buy goods and services.
  • Court cases: when judges decide cases, their decisions guide later cases.
  • Custom: long-standing ways of doing things in a trade or community can also be recognised.
  • The Constitution: the highest law. No contract may go against the rights in the Constitution.

Common contracts on a farm

ContractWho agrees
Employment contractFarmer and worker
LeaseLandowner and person renting land or a house
SaleBuyer and seller of cattle, maize or a bakkie
Supply contractFarm and packhouse or abattoir

When a contract is broken

When one side does not do what was promised, it is called a breach of contract. The other side may ask that the promise is kept, ask for money for the loss (damages), or end the contract. A worker with a problem about an employment contract can ask for help from the CCMA.

Your rights

As a worker you have the right to get the main terms of your work in writing. Keep a copy of every contract you sign in a safe place.

Key points

  • A contract is an agreement that the law will enforce.
  • Both sides must agree, be able to contract, and agree to something legal and possible.
  • Contract law comes from common law, legislation, court cases, custom and the Constitution.
  • Breaking a contract is called a breach.
  • Read every contract before you sign and keep a copy.
